metrics.method: Full history read manually: 166 rows = 157 messages + 9 service events, 2026-06-24 to 2026-09-10. Client side = alias 'Paige (Chey Ref)' (64 msgs) per config/clients.yaml; our side = Vivek 53, Stephski 20, Mica Vecco 6, Michelle Queue 6, Mayson Chat 6, Derrek 2 (93 msgs) per config/team.yaml — no vendor chat team is present in this group. client_questions_total counts distinct client messages posing a question or making an explicit request/report that required a response from us (excludes acknowledgements and replies to our own asks). unanswered_over_24h = the leak link of 2026-09-01 (never answered), the 2026-08-29 second-account fix request (logins supplied, outcome never reported), and the payment confirmations of 2026-07-21 (~36h) and 2026-08-26 (~64h). max_team_silence_days = longest gap between consecutive ALTR messages: 2026-08-04 15:47 to 2026-08-13 10:33 = 8.8d (runners-up 8.1d on 07-07 to 07-15 and 6.5d on 09-02 to 09-09); note the two longest blackouts ended with an invoice and a client-reported outage respectively, never with a proactive update. Promises = explicit commitments by our side ('we will...', 'I'll...', stated cadences); the 3 not counted as kept or lapsed were partially delivered. Remainder of promises_made - kept - lapsed = 3 partial.

what_client_wanted: Visible results she could actually feel — the reason she gave for leaving was outcome, not price or conduct: 'thank you for what you have been doing but its just not working for me I'm sorry!' (2026-09-02). In 70 days we never sent her a single revenue or growth figure to argue against that.
Her Instagram kept alive and unrestricted — she raised account breakages at least six times: 'please help 😂💞' (2026-08-13) and 'i had to change my password again' (2026-08-21).
Her leaked content taken down: 'ive got a leak. someone using my stuff on a swingers website x' (2026-08-31) — she chased the source herself and supplied the link on 2026-09-01.

To be told what's going on and walked through it — she was new to the tooling and said so: 'oh i didnt see this sorry im new to telegram ill do this now x' (2026-07-06), and she responded warmly the one time we explained ourselves at length.
what_worked: Derrek's long-form transparency update about the Instagram guideline changes and the phone-farm investment produced the single warmest message in the entire chat: 'oh wow! thats insane hopefully it works out thank you for updating me 💗 im excited to see where this goes. thank youu. xx' (2026-08-01). One honest, unprompted, substantive update bought more goodwill than ten weeks of templates — and we never sent another.

Vivek's fast hands-on account recovery when he was actually on it: password change reported 05:27:43, fixed and confirmed by 05:34:37 on 2026-08-21, client replied 'perfect thank you so much'. The technical capability was real; only the reporting around it was missing.

Stephski's warm, personal, reliable billing voice — 'my phone number is 4079217561 if you ever need to reach me' (2026-07-01) and 'Its okay! Thats why I ping reminders haha' (2026-07-07). Paige never once pushed back on an invoice and paid five of six cycles; billing tone was a trust asset until the post-resignation chases undid it.
top_fix: Give every client one named account owner who sends an unprompted weekly results update — actual OF revenue and IG growth numbers plus what we did and what broke — and who owns the churn signal. Paige never saw a single number in 70 days, so when she asked herself whether this was working she had nothing but invoices and requests to weigh; the one time we did send a real, substantive update (2026-08-01) she replied with genuine excitement. That same owner would have caught the unreturned boundaries form, the unrouted leak, the 8.8-day blackout, and would have stopped invoicing from sending collection threats to a client who had already resigned.
